title: judged.json — selected.json plus a per-interaction verdict
description: A judged report is a selected report with two keys added, so anything that reads selected.json reads this unchanged. The inherited keys are not re-described here: select_interactions.py already validated them against selected.schema.json, and duplicating that shape would let the two drift. This schema covers only what judging adds.

judge.description: How the judgements were produced, so a surprising verdict can be reproduced or discounted.

tiers.description: Selection tiers that were eligible for judging; everything else was left advisory.

items.description: Interactions actually judged, after the tier filter and the cap.

errors.description: Judgements that failed outright. Recorded as unclear, never dropped silently.

key.description: Identity shared with render_comment.judgement_key, which is how a verdict finds its row.

verdict.description: handled: the boundary is covered here. gap: a reachable state is mishandled or untested. unclear: undetermined, and the default.

citations.description: Citations that resolved against the working tree. A handled or gap verdict cannot reach here with an empty list; verify_citations downgrades it to unclear first.

dropped_citations.description: Citations that did not resolve. Kept rather than discarded: a verdict that cites lines which do not exist is a signal about the judge, not noise.

trail.description: Tool calls the judgement made, for debugging it without re-running it.

error.description: Why this judgement failed, or null. Non-null always pairs with an unclear verdict.
